PullRequest.Title: onboarding: hide spotlights while a modal dialog or the Quick Input is open
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #347989

During the Agents window's first-run tour, the **Choose a workspace** tip stayed on top of the folder trust dialog that **Open Folder...** opens, hiding the dialog's title and the left half of its text. Pressing Escape in that dialog also ended the whole tour, because the spotlight's window-level Escape handler treated it as End Tour. Before the trust dialog, the folder picker (the Quick Input of the simple file dialog) also opened under the tip.

**Before:** the tip covers the trust dialog.

![The Choose a workspace tip covers the title and left half of the folder trust dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca04fd9e-e4e9-4fe2-85b2-70ddf24e6aef)

**Before:** the folder picker opens under the tip.

![The folder picker of Open Folder... renders under the Choose a workspace tip, which stays on screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f872fc7-0a98-49b1-a6ee-bdc4a80cd36c)

## What changed

Onboarding tours and spotlights no longer show while modal UI is visible, a dialog or the Quick Input, and come back when it closes. `SpotlightPresentation` renders every spotlight: scenario tours, sequence steps, guided tryouts, and the chat and sessions spotlights that run through the onboarding service (agent picker, chat input tour, compare agents, inbox auto-advance, archive nudge and others). So the rule lives there, based on `IDialogService` and `IQuickInputService`:

- A step waits for open or queued dialogs and an open Quick Input to close before it starts.
- A visible step hides when a dialog or the Quick Input opens. Hiding removes the callout's listeners, so Escape belongs to that UI. The step keeps listening for its own outcome, so what the user does there can still advance it.
- When the last one closes, the step comes back as it was: same step and counter, its target reopened if the step opens it, and focus back in the callout. Without the backdrop, focus stays where the closed UI returned it.
- A restored step waits briefly (200 ms) and for a pending selection to be decided before it comes back. Modal UI often hands over to more modal UI after a short asynchronous gap: a folder picked in the Quick Input opens the trust dialog, so without the wait the tip would flash between them, or before advancing.
- If what the user did advanced the step, removed its target or made its `when` false, the tour moves on instead of showing an orphaned callout. A missing target follows the step's `missingTarget` behavior (skip, wait or abort). A target click that itself opened the modal UI, such as a **Create Pull Request** action that asks for confirmation, still advances the step, and the next step waits for the modal UI to close.
- Without the backdrop, a step that comes back leaves focus where the user works and doesn't reopen its target, which would take focus.
- The window controls are dimmed again after a dialog closes, since the dialog clears that dimming. The Quick Input dims nothing, so they aren't dimmed while the spotlight steps aside for it.
- An automatic tour doesn't count as shown while modal UI is open: the onboarding service waits for dialogs and the Quick Input before it marks the tour seen, and checks again that it is still eligible.

`OnboardingModalUi` (in `common/`) is the one definition of modal UI, shared by the onboarding service, which decides when a tour may start and count as seen, and `SpotlightPresentation`, which decides what a running spotlight renders. Its observables derive from `IDialogService.hasDialog` and `IQuickInputService.currentQuickInput` and listen to the services only while observed; the service queries them only when a run is about to start, so startup doesn't create the Quick Input controller. Starting a step, hiding it, restoring it and the window dimming all follow those observables, so there are no separate event pairs or flags to keep in sync. Most of the test diff passes the new constructor arguments.

## After

The folder picker opens with the tip out of the way:

![The folder picker of Open Folder... is open and the tour tip is hidden](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52f7abe7-ad94-4025-bdd9-6317f8812255)

The trust dialog is fully readable while the tip stays hidden:

![The folder trust dialog is fully readable and the tour tip is hidden](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9295813f-39f0-457a-a625-7b178fc26347)

After **Cancel**, the tip comes back on the same step (1 of 2) with the workspace picker open again:

![The Choose a workspace tip is back on step 1 of 2 with the workspace picker open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aed40b52-484c-42b4-a2e6-481f1cc6f3a3)

After **Trust Folder & Continue**, the tour moves on to **Choose a model** (2 of 2):

![The tour shows Choose a model, step 2 of 2, after the folder was trusted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e29271ee-e8f5-4071-9b75-996524ff973d)

Another spotlight with an unrelated dialog over it: the **About** dialog opened over **Choose a model** hides the tip, and Escape closes only the dialog:

![The About dialog is open and the Choose a model tip is hidden behind it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76f5d45a-9b55-44f9-8fca-eaefaf1dde9f)

Walkthrough (folder picker and Escape, an untrusted folder from the folder picker through the trust dialog, Trust Folder & Continue, then the Command Palette and the About dialog over the next step, Done):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b18fa5aa-d751-4973-a5ca-38eef5a56444

The sessions list is blurred in the media. Right after Trust Folder & Continue, the new session re-renders the model picker and the **Choose a model** tip re-anchors to it, which shows as a one-frame blink. That is the existing target tracking and isn't changed here.

## How to test

1. Make sure workspace trust is enabled. In a fresh profile the tour shows on its own; otherwise set `"onboarding.developerMode": { "sessions.onboarding.newSessionViewV2": true }` and `"onboarding.developerModeVariations": { "sessions.onboarding.newSessionViewV2": "workspaceAndModel" }`.
2. Open the Agents window. The tour shows **Choose a workspace** (1 of 2).
3. In the workspace picker, select **Open Folder...**. The tip hides while the folder picker is open, and Escape there brings it back.
4. Select **Open Folder...** again and choose a folder that isn't trusted yet. The tip stays hidden through the trust dialog. **Cancel** or Escape brings it back on the same step. **Trust Folder & Continue** moves the tour on to **Choose a model**.
5. Open the Command Palette over **Choose a model**: the tip hides, and comes back when it closes.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` with the 15 affected test files (`spotlightPresentation`, `spotlightOverlay`, `sequencePresentation`, `onboardingPresentationQueue`, `onboardingService`, `guidedTryoutPresentation`, `automationsTour`, `agentsWindowInvitationOnboarding`, `compareAgentsSpotlight`, `newChatWidget`, `sessionsList`, `agentPickerSpotlight`, `sessionArchiveNudge`, `agentHostWorktreeSendChoice`, `modelPickerTabbedWidget`): 1471 passing, 0 failing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --isolate --run` with `spotlightPresentation.test.ts` and `onboardingService.test.ts`: both passed alone (71 and 53 passing).
- The 12 tests in the "modal UI" suite of `spotlightPresentation.test.ts` cover hide and restore with Escape ignored for a dialog and for the Quick Input, the window dimming, advancing on an accepted selection without restoring, a folder picked in the Quick Input whose selection a later dialog decides, target removed, context changed, a target click that opens a dialog, a restore without the backdrop while focus is elsewhere, and no start while a dialog or the Quick Input is open, for tours and sequence steps. They run on virtual time. `onboardingService.test.ts` covers an automatic tour that becomes eligible while the Quick Input is open. Removing each guard makes tests fail: never hiding the step (6 fail), restoring without waiting for a pending selection (1 fails), restoring a step whose target or context moved on (1 fails), starting a sequence step without waiting (2 fail), dropping a queued target click on suspend (1 fails), reopening the target on a non-modal restore (1 fails), and a service that waits only for dialogs (1 fails).
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: no findings.
- Manual: a Code OSS build of this branch, driven with Playwright over CDP, sampling the screen state on every DOM change and frame. The V2 tour with Escape in the folder picker, Cancel, Escape and Trust Folder & Continue on the trust dialog, the Command Palette and the About dialog over the **Choose a model** step, and the V3 sequence tour, whose workspace step advances on a context key. The tip never showed while the folder picker or the trust dialog was open, including the handover between them. Listeners the spotlight adds to the dialog and Quick Input services are removed when the tour ends. The walkthrough above was re-recorded on the previous commit with the same sampling, and the same flow was run again on the latest commit with the same result.
- Manual, for the review follow-ups, in the same Code OSS build. The dialogs, the Command Palette, the services and the spotlight were real; the two small test scenarios and their target buttons were registered at runtime. A target click that opens a confirmation dialog: the tip hides, and after Cancel the tour moves on to step 2 (before the change the clicked step came back). With `onboarding.spotlight.backdrop` off on the first-run tour: after closing the picker, typing in the chat input and closing a dialog, focus and further typing stay in the chat input (before the change the workspace picker reopened and took the keystrokes). An automatic tour that became eligible with the Command Palette open stayed queued and unseen until the palette closed, then showed and was marked seen.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and automatic onboarding becoming eligible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution registers presentations after workbench restoration. Only a queued automatic run reads modal visibility before marking the scenario shown; it waits for modal closure and then rechecks eligibility. Ordinary scenario evaluation does not query currentQuickInput.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: First currentQuickInput read constructs the cached controller, binds context keys/window listeners, and loads stored view state; the actual Quick Input widget remains lazy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per QuickInputService lifetime, only when onboarding is about to run or render, unless another feature already created it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Onboarding did not query Quick Input state; another consumer initialized the controller on first use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous first-use initialization before the tour; not added to unconditional scenario evaluation or initial workbench restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist shown/outcome state and emit existing bounded scenario telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per actual scenario run/impression/outcome, not per modal visibility event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same persistence and telemetry, but only dialogs delayed automatic startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing work is deferred until the automatic run can start; modal waiting does not multiply it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two long-lived OnboardingModalUi instances (service and spotlight presentation), registered scenarios, and at most one running service presentation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The service pump is serial, duplicate scenario IDs join the existing run, and the shared presentation queue serializes per window. Modal waiting is observable/event driven, not polling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Modal event observables cache booleans while observed and detach/reset when unobserved. Quick Input controller initialization is cached for service lifetime. Eligibility/seen-state deduplication remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced contribution construction, eligibility evaluation, queue acquisition, waitForState disposal, and the lazy Quick Input implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured; first-use service initialization depends on whether other workbench features already used Quick Input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. Added visibility checks are lazy and constant-cardinality; intentional waiting does not block unrelated workbench operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting or advancing spotlight tours and sequence steps while dialogs or Quick Input are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A visual step waits for modal closure, then a 200 ms settle interval if it actually waited, before preparation, target resolution, and rendering. With no modal UI it proceeds without the timer. Existing target-resolution polling and finite-animation settling remain bounded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the target DOM, inspect computed style/geometry and ancestor animations, and wait for an animation frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing target resolution per step; restoration adds one readiness/visibility pass after the relevant modal interaction settles. Default target resolution is bounded by 2 seconds, with explicit missingTarget overrides.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same target lookup and animation settling ran when starting/replacing a target, without the new modal gate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Target readiness gates callout rendering; no new filesystem/network work is hidden in the DOM resolver itself.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Sequential visual steps, modal handovers, and the target's ancestor chain; no work per session/history row is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Steps execute sequentially within the per-window presentation slot. A suspended flag permits one restoration task per live shown step; waits are cancellation-aware and do not spin.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Modal boolean observations are shared within the presentation and equality-filter unchanged values. Target resolution intentionally revalidates visibility rather than retaining stale geometry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced runStep, _runPayload, _showStep, the modal helper, target lookup, and animation waits.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The settle delay is explicit; actual modal handover and target animation duration vary. No timing measurements were made.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added delay is the deliberate modal-handover behavior; there is no evidence of an unintended scaling critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Suspending and restoring a visible spotlight, including workspace-picker and model-picker steps
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Suspension removes frame/layout/key listeners immediately. Restoration awaits modal closure and any pending selection, checks current context/target visibility, then reconstructs the callout and optionally reopens its target. Accepted selections advance instead. Non-modal spotlights do not reopen the target when focus is elsewhere.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing initial/final calls, plus a restore call after a dialog closes or two transitions for a Quick Input show/hide pair. No per-workspace/model calls; browser implementation is a no-op.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only initial dimming and final cleanup were requested; dialogs could clear the initial state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Calls are not awaited before rendering or modal handling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate local recent-workspace paths through provider.stat when the workspace picker is reopened.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one stat per eligible local catalog entry per actual reopen, using the existing four-operation Limiter and existing recent/session URI deduplication. No stat cache is added or defeated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scan ran on initial/user-triggered picker opening; the old spotlight did not automatically reopen after modal dismissal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Validation runs fire-and-forget after the picker is rendered; it does not gate spotlight restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/chat/sessionWorkspacePicker.ts: showPicker; browser/agentHostFilterService.ts: rediscover; remoteAgentHost discovery handlers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing optional remote-host rediscovery when a workspace picker is reopened: tunnel enumeration, Mission Control inventory refresh, and cloud refresh-if-stale.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped rediscover per eligible reopen when remote hosts are enabled and discovery is idle, not one per workspace. Registered handlers run concurrently; Mission Control joins its in-flight refresh and cloud uses refresh-if-stale. Desktop tunnel enumeration uses one IPC to listTunnels, then one base network enumeration plus sequential configured-name lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical discovery on ordinary picker opens; automatic restoration introduces another legitimate picker-open trigger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Rediscovery is fire-and-forget and does not gate picker/callout rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-render bounded spotlight content and reopen the model picker from existing model metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reconstruction per restoration. Model-picker instance is reused; markdown resources and step observers/listeners are disposed before replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Callout remained visible rather than being rebuilt after modal UI; picker opening already used the same renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous DOM work at restoration, after modal handling. No model inference/loading is triggered merely by reopening the picker in the traced path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User-driven completed modal interactions during one active step; workspace validation scales with the recent-workspace catalog after existing URI deduplication, and model rendering scales with available models.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One restore task per suspended step; ordinary presentations serialize per window. Workspace stats share a four-slot limiter across reopens. Host discovery is grouped and skipped while already discovering; handler concurrency is not multiplied by workspace count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Overlay DOM shell and model-picker instance are reused; content resources are cleared on reconstruction. Workspace existence checks intentionally remain uncached as on ordinary opens. Remote results/credentials retain existing policies; cloud automatic discovery uses its stale-refresh policy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for restored rendering and transitive boundary counts: traced target.open to workspace/model implementations, filesystem provider.stat, native-host IPC, and grouped discovery handlers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size, remote-host enablement, configured tunnel names, modal frequency, and filesystem/network duration are unknown. All identified extra catalog/discovery work is off the restoration critical path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable regression. Restoration has real additional work, including existing picker-open I/O, but it is tied to the intended reopening behavior, retains existing concurrency controls, and does not establish a pathological new loop/fan-out or blocked important operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ending, cancelling, or replacing a step while modal UI or a target selection is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Step completion disposes its observable reaction and listeners, cancels modal waits/action tokens, and resolves the presentation. Overlay teardown removes DOM and clears pending activation/layout handles. A pending selection may resolve later, but ended guards prevent rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clear native window dimming on overlay disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cleanup request per created backdrop overlay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cleanup request was registered for backdrop overlays.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One live step and at most one queued target activation/restoration task; repeated modal transitions do not accumulate active step subscriptions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: MutableDisposable bounds queued target activation to one timer. DisposableStore owns each step's reactions/listeners, and waitForState removes its subscriptions on resolution or cancellation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: FromEventObservable drops cached state and subscriptions after its last observer. Description rendering disposables are cleared on reuse and disposed with the overlay; target registrations use existing WeakMap/provider ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced done(), cancellation ownership, waitForState cleanup, suspend/hide, activation disposal, and overlay disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Unresolved owner selection promises can outlive a step, but the prior selection callback already awaited those promises; no independently unbounded retention introduced by the diff was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable cleanup or retention regression. The new persistent activation handle is bounded and owned; suspension also stops the existing per-frame target tracking while modal UI is open.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 19 changed files and every diff page, including test-only wiring and the new modal tests. Investigated startup laziness, per-window serialization, restore coalescing, rendering/layout work, cancellation/disposal, native dimming IPC, and transitive picker filesystem/network work. No high-confidence diff-introduced actionable performance regression or qualifying regression-fix provenance identified. Static read-only review; no measurements.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
